android.desc: SMS Forwarder automatically forwards and syncs the SMS messages and push notifications you receive to your PC, a second phone, and other devices. 🚨 CAUTION! 🚨 If someone else asked you to install this app, do not install it. It may be a financial scam such as phishing or smishing. Forwarding your messages to an unknown recipient can expose your personal information. How to use Install the app and create a forwarding rule (filter). You can add multiple filters for different purposes. Enter the recipients (phone number, email, webhook URL, Telegram, or push service ID). Set conditions to include or exclude messages by keyword (in the sender's number or the message content). Customize the template of the forwarded message any way you like. Key Features Multiple destinations: Forward SMS or notifications to email, phone numbers, URLs, Telegram, and the push service. App notifications too: Forward not only SMS but also notifications from apps such as WhatsApp, Messenger, or your banking app. Powerful filtering: Detailed filter options based on the sender's number and the message content. Flexible email support: Full support for Gmail and custom SMTP servers. Dual SIM support: Works with dual SIM devices. Working hours: Set the app to run only when you want, such as during business hours. Backup and restore: Easily back up and restore your filters. Device-to-device sync: Use the push service to exchange messages between devices that have the app installed. Use cases Sharing financial alerts: Automatically share card payment and bank transaction texts with your family. Managing a second phone: Receive all your messages on your main phone or PC without carrying your work phone around. Traveling abroad: Leave the phone with your home SIM at home and still receive its texts by email or Telegram wherever you are. Team notices: Automatically pass important texts on to your team members. Note: This app cannot retrieve messages from devices where the app is not installed. It only forwards messages received on the device running the app. Required permissions We only request the permissions that are essential to the app's core features. RECEIVE_SMS, RECEIVE_MMS, READ_SMS, SEND_SMS Required to read incoming SMS/MMS and forward them

quotes.text:
In other news, I built and deployed a "2FA Mule" last weekend.

It's a stock android phone with no google account and no apps installed except for "SMS Forwarder"[1].

It is configured to forward all SMS to an email address via encrypted SMTP.  This means that I can receive these 2FA codes anywhere I have Internet access - such as an airplane or newly arrived in a foreign country where my SIM card does not work.

The "2FA Mule" itself is plugged in at my office in a corner.

I'm not employing this for anything sensitive but it's interesting to consider that I can use SMS based 2FA while divorcing it from my day to day SIM identity ...

[1] https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.frzinapps.smsforward&hl=en_US&gl=US

quotes.text:
It's been 2 years since I read your initial comment on using an SMS mule [1], and I'm curious how's it going, you know, that phone you have plugged in at your office in a corner :)

No battery swelling?

I copied the idea and did the same, it's essentially free of cost to do so where I live, thanks to having operators that offer a pay-what-you-use tier with no fixed monthly cost. The line is just to act as a 2FA mule, so it means it costs nothing (save causing any kind of expense once every 6 months, but sending a single SMS does it, so I guess it actually costs something like 20cts per year)

Apart from the SMS Forwarder app [2] you suggested, an HN commenter [3] provided links to some FOSS alternative which I didn't get to try but should work fine and is ad-free.

[1]: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=28251107

[2]: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.frzinapps.smsforward

[3]: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=29711030
